name: Poland (Polish People's Republic and Third Polish Republic)

predecessors.name: Second Polish Republic
predecessors.text: the pre-war Polish lands west of the Curzon Line that stayed Polish (Warsaw, Lublin, Kraków, Łódź, Poznań and the rest of central Poland), the overlap of the Second Polish Republic of 1939 and the…

ledger.x: 1945: the Polish state of the Warsaw government begins.
1945: Wartheland passes from Germany to Poland.
1945: the Katowice district passes to Poland.
1945: the Ciechanów district, annexed to East Prussia in 1939, passes to Poland.

1945: the remaining German lands east of the Oder-Neisse line pass under Polish control by the Potsdam Agreement (Danzig, Pomerania west and north of the Vistula and German Upper Silesia are in the January and March gains from nazi-germany above; the gazetteer shows the five voivodeships plus those gains cover all but…
1945, August: the Soviet Union returns the Białystok area to Poland.
1949: the seat of government moves from Łódź to Warsaw.
1952: the Republic of Poland becomes the Polish People's Republic under the July Constitution of 22 July 1952.
1989: the People's Republic ends and the Third Polish Republic begins.

certainty.note: The western frontier is the Oder-Neisse river line, fixed in outline by Potsdam on 2 August 1945 but recognised only by the GDR in 1950 and West Germany in 1970-72; the eastern frontier is the Curzon-line agreement of 16 August 1945.
The German-Polish Border Treaty (signed 14 November 1990, in force 16 January 1992) and the 18 May 1992 confirmation with Ukraine settled every frontier.
